video_title: Blockchain Is Fixing a $2 Trillion Banking Problem with Mike Manning, Juan Montero and Anant
gist: A panel with Avalanche's Mike Manning, Fence Finance CEO Juan Montero and Grove's Anant argues that asset-backed finance and private credit — a $2trn market still run on spreadsheets, PDFs and emails — is the first asset class where blockchain rails produce hard economics: roughly 80% operational cost savings and 30-40% cost-of-capital savings, evidenced by a live BBVA warehouse facility running 300,000 loans a month. The core thesis is that today's tokenization is mostly digital-twin repackaging, and the real unlock is natively on-chain origination plus on-chain life-cycle management, which would have structurally prevented the First Brands and Tricolor double-pledging collapses. All three agree the binding constraint is institutional will and legal plumbing rather than technology or regulation.

insights.claim: Private credit is a roughly $2 trillion market whose operations still run on spreadsheets, PDFs and emails, with settlement weekly or monthly and reporting monthly or quarterly, despite financing credit card receivables, auto loans, invoice finance and merchant cash advances across the real economy.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero (CEO, Fence Finance)
insights.so_what: The gap between the size of the asset class and the primitiveness of its operating stack is the addressable market for private-credit infrastructure vendors — size the opportunity off operational spend, not AUM fees.
insights.quote: Private credit is two trillion dollar market and what surprises people is that this market still runs on spreadsheets, PDFs and emails.

insights.claim: Moving private-credit facility operations from manual processes into software delivers roughly 80% savings in operational cost and up to 40% savings in cost of capital, according to Fence Finance's deployments.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero (CEO, Fence Finance)
insights.so_what: These are the headline economics any private-credit tokenization pitch will be benchmarked against; a platform that cannot show a cost-of-capital delta is selling reporting software, not balance-sheet economics.
insights.quote: We're seeing 80% savings in operational cost. So in timings, as well as up to 40% savings in cost of capital by improving that efficiency.

insights.claim: The hidden cost of manual private-credit operations is negative carry rather than headcount: payments land one week to one month late because reports, borrowing base certificates and covenant compliance checks must be assembled and reconciled by hand, creating idle cash and cash drag.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero (CEO, Fence Finance)
insights.so_what: Cost-of-capital savings in tokenized credit come mostly from eliminating float and idle cash, a durable and quantifiable line item lenders can underwrite.

themes.theme: Asset-backed finance as the natural first mover

insights.claim: Asset-backed finance is the asset category best suited to web3 adoption because blockchain rails directly address its three primary risk vectors — fraud, double pledging and settlement risk — rather than offering a generic efficiency story.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: A clean screening framework: back tokenization ventures that map to one of these three pain points and discount those that don't.
insights.quote: this is the asset category best suited for the adoption of web 3 technology

insights.claim: Securitization is inherently composable finance that has never had a composable technology stack — the underlying loan, the warehouse facility and the securitized notes are linked layers that traditional finance can only reconcile manually.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: Framing tokenization as supplying the missing composable stack for an already-composable product is the argument most likely to land with credit bankers — a useful test of a vendor's go-to-market credibility.
insights.quote: Asset back finance and securization is composable finance without a composable stack.

themes.theme: Fraud, double pledging and the First Brands lesson

insights.claim: The First Brands and Tricolor collapses happened because the same assets were pledged into two different loan pools at once, and 30-, 60- and 90-day lags in applying cash payments to specific loans meant unsynchronized systems let the scheme persist for a long time.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: Cash-to-loan application latency, not credit quality, was the enabling condition for these blowups — screen private-credit lenders on reconciliation frequency as a fraud-detection proxy.
insights.quote: the lack of an immediate linkage between cash and loan activity allowed this to persist for quite a while in kind of a Ponzi scheme

insights.claim: Tokenizing an asset does not prevent double pledging if the token is a digital twin, because the same asset can be pledged on chain and again in a traditional facility; only natively on-chain origination, with loan documents naming the blockchain as the control location, closes the loophole.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: The key diligence question on any RWA product: is this natively issued on chain with legal documents referencing the chain, or a twin carrying the same fraud risk as paper?

insights.claim: Fraud in asset-backed lending can be eliminated by having the obligor digitally sign and attest to the integrity of the underlying loan, making it provable to third parties without relying on the originator's word.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: Obligor-level attestation is the technical prerequisite for verifiable loan tapes — a concrete diligence question for any tokenized-credit platform.

insights.claim: Avalanche's private-credit strategy rests on four pillars — legal enforceability, fiat-to-digital-cash ramps, ratings, and capital — supported by platform partners including Fence, Trunch and Tear, and allocators such as Grove.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: Ratings and fiat ramps are the least-built pillars; a large rated on-chain deal would be the concrete signal that this thesis is inflecting.

themes.theme: Capital velocity and the capital-light originator

insights.claim: If loans are originated on chain and money moves on chain, an originator can pledge loan by loan instead of warehousing a week's production, collapsing its balance sheet requirement from a week's worth of origination to a single loan's worth.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: This is the clearest quantifiable ROE improvement in the thesis — a lender's equity requirement falls by roughly the ratio of a week's production to one loan.
insights.quote: Now my balance sheet as an originator drops from a week's worth of production to one loan's worth of production.

insights.claim: Instant conditional funding turns fintech lending from a capital-intensive to a capital-light model and makes economically viable assets with one- to three-day duration that could never survive traditional warehouse settlement lags.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero (CEO, Fence Finance)
insights.so_what: Watch for new short-duration credit products — trade and acquisition finance, sub-week receivables — that only become financeable once settlement is instantaneous.
insights.quote: it turns a capital inensive model into a capital light model

insights.claim: Collapsing the money rail and the asset rail onto the same technology stack is the actual source of the efficiency gain, because it removes the gap between asset creation and cash movement that forces originators to balance-sheet production.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: Use 'do money and assets settle on the same rail?' as the test separating real capital-efficiency plays from reporting-layer tokenization.
insights.quote: collapsing the money rail and the asset rail on the same tech stack and what that unlocks is very very significantly accelerated capital velocity

insights.claim: Grove moved from tokenized treasury bills to placing roughly $250 million of Janus Henderson AAA CLOs on Avalanche, aiming to bring off-chain yield on chain and dampen the volatility of crypto-backed lending markets.
insights.speaker: Anant (investments and product, Grove)
insights.so_what: Real-world credit is being used as a volatility dampener for on-chain lending rates — a structural and growing bid for short-duration institutional credit product from crypto balance sheets.

insights.claim: Grove's key capital-efficiency innovation is borrowing alongside its investments rather than sequentially: instead of buying the first $100 of assets and then borrowing $98, it contributes $2 of equity and draws the senior facility simultaneously via codified smart contracts.
insights.speaker: Anant (investments and product, Grove)
insights.so_what: Simultaneous equity-and-senior deployment removes drag at the fund level and is a replicable structure for any levered on-chain credit allocator.

insights.claim: The bottleneck in on-chain credit has shifted from lenders to originators: capital willing to lend on chain already exists, and what is missing is end-to-end originators that both originate assets on chain and borrow against them on chain.
insights.speaker: Anant (investments and product, Grove)
insights.so_what: Supply of on-chain-native collateral, not demand for it, is the scarce input — origination platforms are the constrained asset in this value chain.
insights.quote: I mean I think the lenders are here. So I think what we're really looking for is that end to end originators to originate assets that are onchain and borrow against them onchain.

themes.theme: The BBVA facility as proof point

insights.claim: Fence Finance put a BBVA warehouse facility's loan agreement into software for a portfolio originating 300,000 loans per month, delivering real-time covenant and performance visibility on a book far past the point where spreadsheets can cope.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero (CEO, Fence Finance)
insights.so_what: A named tier-one bank running a live 300k-loans-per-month facility on this stack is the strongest available evidence that production adoption has begun rather than piloting.

insights.claim: For an earned-wage-access originator with 10-25 day receivables, waiting a week for the bank's loan operations team to disburse would raise cost of capital by roughly 60% — hundreds of thousands of dollars per facility — and BBVA won the mandate specifically because it could offer capital on demand.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero (CEO, Fence Finance)
insights.so_what: Settlement speed is becoming a competitive weapon in warehouse lending mandates; banks without instant disbursement will lose short-duration receivables business on price.
insights.quote: the cost the cost of capital will be increased by around like 60%. So it's a crazy number.

insights.claim: The BBVA deployment saved roughly 80% of operational cost on both the bank's back and middle office and the fintech originator's side, cut 30-40% of total cost of capital, and seeded a business that has since reached $1.5 billion in assets under administration.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero (CEO, Fence Finance)
insights.so_what: $1.5bn AUA is a concrete traction benchmark for the private-credit infrastructure category, and because savings accrue to both counterparties the referral dynamics should compound.

insights.claim: The binding constraint on institutional adoption is will rather than technology or regulation, because on-chain deals replicate existing legal structures rather than creating new ones — controllable electronic records, securities entitlements and depository tokens already exist and lawyers understand them.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: If regulation is not the gate, the catalyst to watch is deal flow rather than rulemaking — a few large rated on-chain deals should trigger a fast-follower wave.
insights.quote: The legal frameworks are here cuz and here's the key is we're not creating new structures. We're just replicating existing structures on chain. This is the rails, not the substance.

insights.claim: Issuing a private-credit asset as an NFT is a red flag because an NFT is not legally enforceable in court, unlike established wrappers such as controllable electronic records or securities entitlements.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: A fast negative screen for RWA deals: NFT-wrapped credit assets signal legal naivety and should be discounted heavily.
insights.quote: A board ape is not legally enforceable in a court of law. That's always a red flag for me when I hear people saying they're issuing an NFT.

insights.claim: All three panelists agree that most tokenization today is repackaging — putting a digital twin on chain — rather than genuine rebuilding, though Grove's Anant expects that to change within six to nine months, and adoption is expected to be reflexive because everyone wants to be first to be third.
insights.speaker: Anant, Juan Montero and Mike Manning
insights.so_what: Insiders concede the current RWA wave is mostly cosmetic; the six-to-nine-month window for natively on-chain issuance is the timeline against which to test the thesis, and adoption should arrive non-linearly rather than gradually.
insights.quote: most organization is just repackaging putting a digital twin on chain

insights.claim: The on-chain credit industry is building leveraging platforms when it needs lending platforms that finance the real economy rather than merely levering existing assets.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: A critique that separates sustainable on-chain credit businesses from reflexive leverage stacks — favour platforms whose collateral originates from real-economy lending.
insights.quote: I think the industry right now is building leveraging platforms we need to start bringing building lending platforms we need to finance the real economy not just lever it up

themes.theme: Chain choice and the on-chain boundary

insights.claim: The prevailing 'opportunity through optionality' approach of supporting 150-plus chains institutionalizes fragmentation, and the industry should instead pursue 'distribution through depth', consolidating around roughly five to six chains to build liquidity; institutions care less which chain an asset sits on than who else is in the room.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: If institutional RWA activity consolidates onto five or six chains, winner-take-most dynamics at the chain level matter more than technical differentiation.
insights.quote: It's not going to be one chain. It's not going to be 100. It's going to be something in the five to six range.

insights.claim: For value and cash movement, the decisive chain-selection criteria are resilience and uptime — avoiding single or few points of failure where a controlling party could stop supporting the service — plus security and depth of ecosystem tooling such as on- and off-ramps.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero and Anant
insights.so_what: Centralization risk is becoming an explicit procurement criterion for institutional chain selection, which disadvantages permissioned bank-owned chains over time.

insights.claim: Fence's position is that roughly 90-95% of what belongs on chain is money and asset flows, while items a smart contract cannot resolve — audited financial accounts, change-of-control covenants on the originator or servicer — must stay in the legal layer, whereas Manning argues every life-cycle event including transferring the servicer can eventually execute on chain if properly defined in the documents.
insights.speaker: Juan Montero and Mike Manning
insights.so_what: Sets realistic expectations for on-chain private credit as a hybrid legal-plus-code architecture; the unresolved disagreement determines how much of the servicing fee pool is actually automatable.
insights.quote: I think like what should be put into smart contracts is money flows and value flows.

insights.claim: A facility's credit buy box can be encoded in a smart contract that automatically accepts or rejects not-yet-originated future receivables on arrival, and covenants such as a loan falling out of the borrowing base after a 15-day missed payment can be implemented on chain.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: Automated eligibility screening at the point of receivable intake is the mechanism that makes continuous borrowing-base management possible — the core technical claim to validate.

insights.claim: On-chain settlement can be asset-by-asset rather than gross: a buy-now-pay-later consumer payment arriving as a stablecoin is applied directly to the individual loan, amortizing it and immediately pushing the stablecoin back out for redeployment into another loan.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning (head of institutional finance, Avalanche)
insights.so_what: Loan-level cash application is where capital efficiency beyond operational automation comes from, and it is also the structural fix for the reconciliation lag that hid the First Brands fraud.
insights.quote: It's getting applied directly against that one loan, not against the pool as a whole, but mapped to that particular loan

insights.claim: Underwriting and deal structuring should never be delegated to smart contracts because they require judgment and bespoke flexibility, with code handling roughly 99% and flagging the remaining 1%; personally identifiable information also remains an unresolved constraint on what can move on chain.
insights.speaker: Mike Manning and Anant
insights.so_what: Draws the boundary of the addressable market: this is settlement and operations software, so credit-judgment franchises and their fee streams are not being disrupted, and privacy tooling remains an open venture gap.
insights.quote: This is a settlement and operational technology. It's not a judgment technology.
